international.title: The life, death and improbable rebirth of LA’s most beloved diner
international.summary: For decades, it served pancakes, hash browns and steaks to hungry Angelenos. Then came closure, and a city mourned – but now the Original Pantry is back Sometimes, an old-school American diner is just a diner. And sometimes, like the Original Pantry in downtown Los Angeles, it feels like the heart and soul of a city, a bellwether of good times and bad. For decades it was famous for never closing. Located in a low-slung shotgun building on a busy corner, it fed politicians, movie stars, students, criminals and street bums around the clock, seven days a week. The doors had no locks, because the place had no need for them. The portions were huge, the prices dirt cheap, and many of the servers, in bow ties and white shirts, looked like extras from a Harold Lloyd two-reeler. Continue reading...
